cases.title: TIBU-13977: Add Log Failure messages for miscellaneous errors on TVM
cases.custom_steps:
I do not believe the log failure part of the below have been implemented yet.

If any of the validation checks fail on the TVM then the TVM will attempt to POST a message to the Log Failure API (see section 3.9.1) with the message “Invalid <Field that Failed Validation (ProductId, StartPointId or EndPointId)> for booking reference <BookingReference field from Validate response>”.

If printing fails for any reason then when the Print Fail error screen is displayed it will also trigger the device to attempt to POST a message to the Log Failure API (see section 3.9.1) with the message “Print failed for booking reference <BookingReference field from Validate response>”.

Acceptance Criteria


GIVEN that a booking reference is being validated that has an invalid field (i.e. product, boarding stop, alighting stop)

WHEN the booking reference is submitted

THEN the relevant error screen is displayed

AND a message is sent to the Log Failure API (see section 3.9.1) with the message “Invalid <Field that Failed Validation (ProductId, StartPointId or EndPointId)> for booking reference <BookingReference field from Validate response>”

 

GIVEN that a booking reference has been validated successfully

AND the printer is in an error state (i.e. no paper, not connected, jammed)

WHEN the “Print Ticket” button is selected

THEN the print failure screen is displayed

AND a message is sent to the Log Failure API (see section 3.9.1) with the message “Print failed for booking reference <BookingReference field from Validate response>”

cases.title: TIBU-13697: As a TVM user I would like the printed smartcard tickets to include the necessary collect ticket information
cases.custom_steps:
This ticket is specfically to make sure ticket formats that contain smartcard information (such as half fare, yLink, 24+ or concession tickets) and the smartcard related fields (i.e. Card No. and Expiry Date) are hidden.

The ticket that is printed is determined by the ticket assignment for the product that was calculated during the “Validation” section (from the ProductId in the Validation API response). Given that the product may not be from the same branch of the operator hierarchy as the TVM home location it must still be possible for the TVM to access the ticket formats necessary to print these products.

These tickets may have the following dynamic fields (as explained in reference [1]) which will be populated on top of the base ticket template:

Booking Reference - <Booking Reference of redeemed ticket>.

Payment Type - “COLL”

Outbound Time - For Type U - if different to 00:00 then <Time from ValidOnTime field of Validate response> otherwise do not display field and shift remainder of the ticket up a line. TIBU-14395 - AC1 - Ensure multi-use barcodes use UTC time on TVMs
cases.custom_steps:
The time zone used for times in the multi-use barcodes was not specified and currently uses local time which may cause issues around the clock change. As such we need to adjust the encoded Start Time and Expiry Time on the barcode to be in UTC and adjust the validation mechanism to handle the Start Time and Expiry time in UTC

__Acceptance Criteria__:


1. If the Expiry Type is populated but the Expiry Value is 0 then the encoded Expiry Date & Time should be 4am the next day - NIR Adult Day Return is a good example for this

2. If the Expiry Type is configured with a time period greater than “Hours” and Expiry Value is configured with a value greater than 0 then the encoded Expiry Date & Time should be 4am on the day after the date calculated as the expiry date - NIR Adult Weekly Season is a good example for this (i.e. Bought on 4th May 2024, 1 week expiry configured, expiry date calculated as 10th May so encoded Expiry Date & Time is “2405110400”)

3. If the Expiry Type is configured with a time period less than or equal to “Hours” and Expiry Value is configured with a value greater than 0 then the encoded Expiry Date & Time should matches exactly the result of the expiry calculation - Glider Adult Single is a good example for this (i.e. Bought on 4th May 2024 13:00, 90 minutes expiry configured, expiry date calculated as 4th May 2024 14:30 so encoded Expiry Date & Time is “2405041430”

4. The only exception to the above rules is for barcode redemptions/ticket collection where the Barcode Type is S or H. These should use 4am on the day after the “Inbound Date” from the integrated barcode API for the Expiry Date & Time.

5. If 3 day select product is purchased then the Start Time is encoded as 4am on the first day of validity, Additional dates is an offset from the start date as specified previously, Expiry Time is 4am on the 3rd day of validity.


6. If Type D (3 Day Select) barcode is redeemed then the Start Time is encoded as 4am on ValidOnDate1, Additional dates is an offset from the start date as specified previously, Expiry Time is 4am on ValidOnDate3.

Then in validation we are checking that the current date time is either within 1 day from Start Time (4am Start Date to 4am the next day), within 1 day from Start Time plus Offset (4am Start Date plus offset to 4am the next day) or within 1 day from Expiry Time (4am Expiry Date to 4am the next day).


Note that the above examples are in the topology “MUB Scenarios”.

Description

Barcode printing of the previous format has already been implemented on TVM so should be a case of verifying that it still works with the new encoding and ensuring that we have all the necessary ticket template files.

Note that the below is the original requirement for this functionality but essentially, if the “Print Barcode” product setting for the product that is being purchased is set to true then a multiple use barcode should be printed at the end of the ticket. If it is false then a barcode is not printed on the ticket and there should be no white space at the end of the ticket for where the barcode could have gone.

Note that the gap between the end of the ticket and the barcode should be roughly as shown in the Multiple Use Barcode specification.

The barcode itself should be encoded with all of the product information that corresponds to the ticket that is being purchased.

REQ-0095.4 - Print Barcodes on Tickets - essentially printing multi use barcodes

The device shall be capable of printing a barcode (in the Aztec Code format) on a ticket.

Applies to:
ETM (All)
HHD (All)
POS (All)
TVM (All)

Constraint:
CloudFare will provide the option for Translink users to select whether or not a barcode should be printed for each individual paper ticket type. (REQ-1750.23) 
The device will  append a barcode onto the end of the ticket, if configured. Flowbird consider this to be the optimum location for presentation of the barcode to a validation device. By appending the barcode to the end of the ticket it also allows the position of the barcode to be automatically adjusted for tickets that have variable length fields that can span one or many lines on the ticket 
The space between the end of the ticket and the barcode will be determined by Translink via the use of a single example in their ticket template document  (REQ-3522.0)
If an individual ticket is being produced for multiple passengers the device will not encode a barcode on the ticket

Acceptance Criteria


GIVEN I have selected a ticket that is configured to print a barcode

WHEN that ticket is purchased

THEN the corresponding ticket is printed

AND at the end of the ticket a multiple use barcode is printed

cases.title: TIBU-19121: Remove all TL80 templates on a topology update
cases.custom_steps:
Description

A topology update contains the ticket templates in ini format, as it is used on IML5 printers.
When using TL80 printers, a conversion takes place, where the templates are converted to an appropriate format (.xml) and stored in a specific location on the hard drive. These templates are then retained for future use.

A dataset update typically removes all templates as the C:\tvm folder gets reset

A topology update currently does NOT remove the TL80 templates, which means that older templates from previous  deployments may remain in the system 

 

We need to ensure, that, upon a topology update, the TL80 templates are purged so that we can rebuild them using the updated templates

Environment


None
Closure Reason


None
Requirements


None
Attachments
1

I would go about testing it as follows:

1. Deploy the version onto a Kiosk

2. Print a set of tickets. Take note of the templates used to print them (you can find them in the gfts logs - the name may map to a template with a different name - check C:/tvm/modele/miml5/modmiml5.ini)

cases.title: TIBU-16970 - As a customer I want my Bus Kiosk to be capable of printing a barcode on a ticket
cases.custom_steps:
This has already been implemented on Rail Retail Kiosk but ticket formats for bus will need to be updated for this as well as adding support for bus specific fields (i.e. Boarding/Alighting Stop should be Scheme ID instead of Stage ID).

Note that the below is the original requirement for this functionality but essentially, if the “Print Barcode” product setting for the product that is being purchased is set to true then a multiple use barcode should be printed at the end of the ticket. If it is false then a barcode is not printed on the ticket and there should be no white space at the end of the ticket for where the barcode could have gone.

Note that the gap between the end of the ticket and the barcode should be roughly as shown in the Multiple Use Barcode specification.

The barcode itself should be encoded with all of the product information that corresponds to the ticket that is being purchased.

REQ-0095.4 - Print Barcodes on Tickets - essentially printing multi use barcodes

The device shall be capable of printing a barcode (in the Aztec Code format) on a ticket.

Applies to:
ETM (All)
HHD (All)
POS (All)
TVM (All)

Constraint:
CloudFare will provide the option for Translink users to select whether or not a barcode should be printed for each individual paper ticket type. (REQ-1750.23) 
The device will  append a barcode onto the end of the ticket, if configured. Flowbird consider this to be the optimum location for presentation of the barcode to a validation device. By appending the barcode to the end of the ticket it also allows the position of the barcode to be automatically adjusted for tickets that have variable length fields that can span one or many lines on the ticket 
The space between the end of the ticket and the barcode will be determined by Translink via the use of a single example in their ticket template document  (REQ-3522.0)
If an individual ticket is being produced for multiple passengers the device will not encode a barcode on the ticket

 

NOTE: As mentioned at the top of this story, the key differences in the encoding are as follows:

Mode could be “All” (FFFF) or “Bus” (0001) - this should already be implemented as it should just use the value set in CloudFare but should be tested on bus

Boarding Location will use the “Scheme Id” of the boarding map point will be used rather than the “Stage Id” (do not believe this has been implemented yet)

Alighting Location will use the “Scheme Id” of the boarding map point will be used rather than the “Stage Id” (do not believe this has been implemented yet)

Description

Discovered during testing TIBU-19259: TVM - CR116 - Ensure previous date is printed on tickets if expiry time is between midnight and 4am
Customer Test

AND the calculated expiry time is 04:00 on Day 1
WHEN the ticket is printed
THEN the valid date on the ticket shows Day 0
AND Day 1 at 04:00 is encoded in the barcode expiry date
For type U barcodes it does not count seconds, which means the valid date on ticket will be Day 0 if calculated expiry time is 4:00am

For type E and B it counts seconds so almost always 4:00:ssam will be later than 4:00:00am and Day1 will be printed.

cases.title: TIBU-22094 - yLink tickets "Route" field will display "TVMUB" [INC0384989]
cases.custom_steps:
There appears to be an issue with the route displayed on 300 yLink tickets as "Route" field will display "TVMUB" rather than the route number. This is the case for both directions (Grand Central – Int Airport and Int Airport – Grand Central) and for both payment types. 300 Return, Single and Monthly tickets are displaying the route number as expected:

yLink Single on 300 route showing Route as TVM home location (TVMUb):

Standard 300 tickets displaying route number as expected:

Other routes appear to be displaying as expected, I checked the 9 and 5f both which printed with the route number as expected:

I will raise both on the priority list

--------------------------------------------------

Bit of an update on the route issue from 5.3.1 after further testing.

It appears the issue happens when you switch boarding stage to one different from the location set on TVM. For example, setting our test Kiosk to Laganside location then switching stages to set the boarding or alighting stage to BGCS and issuing a yLink ticket will display the "TVMUb" route issue.

Please see examples below:

Scenario 1 With TVM Location set to "Laganside" PTI:

Insert yLink smartcard into smartcard reader
Change boarding stage to Belfast Grand Central Station
Change alighting stage to any other applicable stage
Issue ticket and check "Route" field, expecting it will incorrectly display "TVMUb"
Transaction sent to quarantine in CF

Scenario 2 With TVM Location set to "Laganside" PTI:

Insert yLink smartcard into smartcard reader
Change boarding stage to any applicable stage that will have BGCS as valid alighting stage (use International Airport for example)
Change alighting stage to BGCS
Issue ticket and check "Route" field, expecting it will incorrectly display "TVMUb"
Transaction sent to quarantine in CF

TVM set to Laganside with Laganside set as selecting boarding stage, correct route will display:

See similar examples below with TVM PTI location changed to Belfast Grand Central with dummy stage:

With TVM location set to BGCS, place yLink card in smartcard reader
Select BGCS as boarding or alighting stage
Issue ticket, route will display correctly on ticket and transaction audited as expected in back office:

TVM set to BGCS location but boarding stage changed to Laganside:

These are the only examples spotted so far but would guess its consistent across the board in terms of setting a different boarding/alighting stage to the location of TVM and issuing a yLink ticket. Not sure if this is linked to the BGCS dummy stage but might be worthwhile having a quick chat to Kerry about this if you think it could be the problem?

Hopefully this additional information helps with investigations. This issue is seen as a blocker due to the fact transactions are hitting quarantine.
